- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) and recent prices are trending up — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (especially <0.2) — model is overly cautious.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sharp spikes — adjust for momentum lag.
- After a price spike (e.g., >+2% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion bias: model frequently forecasts prices to revert to historical mean (e.g., 76–78 range) too early — defer correction until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating 0.27/0.36), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecasts with weighted average of 3–5 prior days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts late-period prices (last 7–10 days) — reduce forecast tail by 5–10% if sentiment is weak or flat.
